findings.summary: The classification leaves out steward Proposals, which are most of the steward's requests and the class the owner's exclusion sentence assumes are fixes. The reason given for rejecting the simpler, correct rule is already handled by the plan's own guard.
findings.evidence: steward.rs:1045-1048 maps every model item except RepeatedFailure to `WorkItemKind::Proposal`. The model's BlindSpot items go through `blind_spot_change` (steward.rs:969-, 754-765). So the steward's root-cause and other Athena fixes are all Proposals, and `is_fix_request` never flags them. The request says 'Website and study content requests from the steward are not fixes'. The accepted reading says 'A steward Proposal that touches only website or studies/ content is not a fix'. Both imply that other steward requests are fixes. Under the plan's rule no steward Proposal is a fix, so both exclusions remove nothing. The plan rejects the steward-channel rule because 'it includes the steward's website and study content requests', but decision 4 already adds a request-text guard that removes exactly those. Only the steward writes the `steward` channel (steward.rs:660-683 is the only `REQUEST_CHANNEL` writer, read by `improvement_requests`, steward.rs:376-384). The plan says itself that the share of the 52 requests it covers was not measured. Fix: Classify a request as a fix when either (a) it is an open steward-channel request (`steward::improvement_requests`) whose own text does not touch only content paths, or (b) it is one of Hestia's waiting root-cause requests (`cause_jobs`) or gate-review requests (`fix_requests_of`). The content guard reads `request_text_touches(request.text)`. A request that names only `studies/` or the site's content files is not a fix. Decide and state which xtask/site paths count as website content; generator code can stay a fix. Drop the work-item lookup through the last job evidence (decision 3) and its `steward::decide` order test: the channel already identifies the steward's requests. Update the criterion 3 test to queue a steward-channel request with studies-only text and show it is not flagged. Update the criterion 4 test to show that a steward Proposal-made request naming `crates/` is ranked first. In D181, drop the 'Proposals are not ranked' limitation, or replace it with the content-path rule.
findings.location: Decision 2 (and its rejected alternative 'Treat every steward-channel request as a fix'), Decision 3, Risks bullet 2

findings.summary: The content guard covers only `studies/`, but the owner also excludes website content.
findings.evidence: The plan treats all of `xtask/` and `.github/workflows/pages.yml` as Athena code (decision 4, rejected alternative 'Treat all of OUTCOME_PATHS as content'; OUTCOME_PATHS at drain.rs:478). The request names 'Website and study content requests'. A steward request that edits only site page text would therefore be ranked as a fix. Fix: Name the paths that hold website content, as distinct from generator logic, and add them to the guard. If none can be separated from code, say so in D181 and add a test showing which side a site-only request falls on.

findings.summary: The cap-slot consequence is close to the out-of-scope item 'changing ... urgent/high caps' and should be stated to the owner plainly.
findings.evidence: `build_capped` hands out high slots in plan order (plan.rs:811-818, 847-865). With the flag in the key, a non-person high feature request can now be demoted to normal in favor of a high fix request. Hestia's root-cause requests are queued at High (hestia.rs:1012-1014), so this case will occur. Fix: Keep the choice, but put the consequence in the CHANGELOG entry and the `athena drain --help` text, not only in D181, so the owner sees that the cap values are unchanged but which item holds a slot can change.

summary: The core change is sound. I checked plan.rs:767-787: the sort at line 783 only sees ready, dependency-free items of the best effective priority, so the key `(!e.fix, e.rung, age)` cannot beat a priority, a cap or a dependency. Every plan goes through drain.rs:2367 into `build_improving`, `build_capped` and `build_with`, so both `athena plan` and `athena drain` get the rule. The dependents list, the serde skip, the wording updates and the tests are thorough. The classification is the problem. The plan ranks only steward work items of kind BlindSpot or RepeatedFailure. In the code, the steward's model-written items of every kind except RepeatedFailure become `Proposal` (steward.rs:1045-1048). Only the code-built blind spot (steward.rs:754-765) and model RepeatedFailure items keep their kind. Every other steward request, including the steward's root-cause fixes, is never ranked. The owner's sentence "Website and study content requests from the steward are not fixes" only makes sense if steward requests count as fixes by default. The reading says the same: "A steward Proposal that touches only website or studies/ content is not a fix". Under this plan, that exclusion never has anything to remove. The plan rejected the simpler rule (every steward-channel request, minus content-only ones) because it "includes the steward's website and study content requests". But the plan's own request-text guard already removes those. That simpler rule also makes the fragile "last job evidence" link (decision 3) unnecessary, since only the steward writes to the steward channel (steward.rs:676, the only `REQUEST_CHANNEL` writer). As planned, the owner's stated goal (52 starved steward requests) is likely to be largely unmet, and the plan admits it did not measure how many it covers. Revise the classification. The rest of the plan can stay.
